title: From Data to Action: 10 Years of Impact with FDI’s Oral Health Observatory
html:
The oral health observatory impact report is now available in French and Spanish! Learn more about the details of the report in a dedicated podcast episode. Listen and share now.

As part of the continued dissemination of the Oral Health Observatory (OHO) 10 Years Impact Report, FDI has developed and released French and Spanish versions of the report, opening up the findings to a broader international audience and supporting greater exchange across oral health communities.

Alongside the new language editions, FDI has also launched a new episode of The Dental Check-Up Podcast dedicated to the report, creating a dialogue around 10 years of oral health data. Featuring Prof. Sarah Baker and Prof. Georgios Tsakos, members of the OHO Task Team, the conversation explores key questions emerging from OHO’s journey, including the main challenges of collecting practice-based data and how the OHO survey differs from traditional, national oral health surveys.

The discussion also highlights an important finding from the data: even in countries where positive oral hygiene and lifestyle behaviours are reported, oral diseases remain prevalent and chronic. This points to a wider challenge for oral health systems that are still largely structured around treating patients, rather than supporting the long-term management and prevention of oral conditions.

The podcast complements the report and helps explore what OHO’s 10 years of data can tell us about the future of oral health research, policy and advocacy.

OHO Podcast – Ten Years of Oral Health Data

FDI thanks Haleon for their support in the development of the OHO 10-year impact report. 

  • Oral Health Observatory 10 Years of Oral Health Observatory Data Report

    The report draws on more than a decade of practice-based data collected from over 10,000 patients across 12+ countries. It demonstrates how point-of-care oral health data can inform policy dialogue, research, and advocacy.
